paper_title: Weak compactons of nonlinearly dispersive KdV and KP equations (Anco, 2024, Studies in Applied Mathematics)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
The profile weak forms are not additional assumptions; they are exactly the traveling-wave reductions of the PDE weak forms. For the one-dimensional equation, a compactly supported profile \(U\) with \(g=c\) satisfies
\[
W_K(U):=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)\phi' + bU^n\phi'''\right)d\xi=0
\quad\text{for all }\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)
\]
if and only if \(u(t,x)=U(x-ct)\) satisfies the weak \(K(m,n)\) identity. For the two-dimensional equation, a line profile with
\[
\xi=x+\mu y-\nu t,
\qquad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2
\]
satisfies
\[
W_{KP}(U):=\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)\phi'' + bU^n\phi''''\right)d\xi=0
\quad\text{for all }\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)
\]
if and only if \(u(t,x,y)=U(x+\mu y-\nu t)\) satisfies the weak line-wave \(KP(m,n)\) identity after integrating out the passive coordinates.

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\iint_{\mathbb R^2}\left(u\psi_t+au^m\psi_x+bu^n\psi_{xxx}\right)dtdx=0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\iiint_{\mathbb R^3}\left(u\psi_{tx}+\sigma u\psi_{yy}+au^m\psi_{xx}+bu^n\psi_{xxxx}\right)dtdxdy=0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &u(t,x)=U(\xi),\quad \xi=x-ct,\quad g=c.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &u(t,x,y)=U(\xi),\quad \xi=x+\mu y-\nu t,
\quad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\partial_t=\partial_\tau-c\partial_\xi,
\quad \partial_x=\partial_\xi\quad\text{under (P3).}\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\partial_t=\partial_\tau-\nu\partial_\xi,
\quad \partial_x=\partial_\xi,
\quad \partial_y=\partial_\zeta+\mu\partial_\xi\quad\text{under (P4).}\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\psi\text{ is smooth and compactly supported, so total }\tau\text{- and }\zeta\text{-derivatives integrate to zero.}
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For \(K(m,n)\), use (P3)--(P5) in (P1):
\begin{align}
0&=\iint \left(U(\psi_\tau-c\psi_\xi)+aU^m\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi\\
&=\iint \left((-cU+aU^m)\psi_\xi+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi
\qquad\text{by (P7).}
\end{align}
Since test functions of the separated form \(\psi(\tau,\xi)=\eta(\tau)\phi(\xi)\), with \(\int\eta d\tau=1\), are admissible after compact support localization, this is equivalent to
\begin{align}
\int_{\mathbb R}\left((-gU+aU^m)\phi'+bU^n\phi'''\right)d\xi=0.
\end{align}
For \(KP(m,n)\), use (P4)--(P6):
\begin{align}
\psi_{tx}&=\psi_{\tau\xi}-\nu\psi_{\xi\xi},\\
\psi_{yy}&=\psi_{\zeta\zeta}+2\mu\psi_{\zeta\xi}+\mu^2\psi_{\xi\xi},\\
\psi_{xx}&=\psi_{\xi\xi},
\qquad \psi_{xxxx}=\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}.
\end{align}
The terms \(U\psi_{\tau\xi}\), \(U\psi_{\zeta\zeta}\), and \(U\psi_{\zeta\xi}\) integrate to zero by (P7), because \(U\) is independent of \(\tau\) and \(\zeta\). Hence
\begin{align}
0&=\iiint \left((-(\nu-\sigma\mu^2)U+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi d\zeta\\
&=\iiint \left((-gU+aU^m)\psi_{\xi\xi}+bU^n\psi_{\xi\xi\xi\xi}\right)d\tau d\xi d\zeta.
\end{align}
Again testing with separated compactly supported functions reduces this identity exactly to \(W_{KP}(U)=0\).

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
W_K(U)\Longleftrightarrow u(t,x)=U(x-ct)\text{ is a weak traveling compacton profile},\quad g=c,\\
W_{KP}(U)\Longleftrightarrow u(t,x,y)=U(x+\mu y-\nu t)\text{ is a weak line compacton profile},\quad g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_2:
\section*{Claim}
Let
\[
F(U):=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'',
\qquad
A_1:=bU^n,
\quad A_2:=b(U^n)',
\quad A_3:=F(U),
\quad A_4:=F(U)'.
\]
For \(U_c(\xi)=U(\xi)H(L-|\xi|)\), the weak cutoff test is the finite endpoint trace test
\[
K(m,n):\quad F'=0\text{ on }(-L,L),\quad A_1=A_2=A_3=0\text{ at }\pm L,
\]
and
\[
KP(m,n):\quad F''=0\text{ on }(-L,L),\quad A_1=A_2=A_3=A_4=0\text{ at }\pm L.
\]
If \(U(\xi)\sim U_0(L-|\xi|)^p\), \(U_0\ne0\), then the \(K(m,n)\) endpoint condition is exactly \(p>2/n\). The \(KP(m,n)\) endpoint condition is \(p>2/n\) plus exactly one of the six leading-power alternatives displayed in the final result.

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &s:=L-|\xi|,\qquad U\sim U_0s^p,
\qquad U_0\ne0,
\qquad m,n>0,
\qquad a,b\ne0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &U_c=UH(L-|\xi|),\qquad H^q=H\quad(q>0).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\int fH\phi^{(r)}d\xi
=(-1)^r\int f^{(r)}H\phi d\xi+\text{endpoint traces involving }\phi,\ldots,\phi^{(r-1)}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\phi(\pm L),\phi'(\pm L),\phi''(\pm L),\phi'''(\pm L)
\text{ are independently prescribable by }C_c^\infty\text{ tests.}\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &s^q\to0\text{ as }s\to0^+\Longleftrightarrow q>0.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &A_4\sim -gpU_0s^{p-1}+apmU_0^m s^{pm-1}+bpn(pn-1)(pn-2)U_0^n s^{pn-3}.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
For \(K(m,n)\), integration by parts gives
\begin{align}
\int\left((-gU_c+aU_c^m)\phi'+bU_c^n\phi'''\right)d\xi
&=-\int F'(U)H\phi d\xi
-\left(\phi''A_1-\phi'A_2+\phi A_3\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
Thus the identity holds for all \(\phi\) exactly when \(F'=0\) inside the support and \(A_1,A_2,A_3\) vanish at both endpoints. For \(KP(m,n)\), the same calculation one order higher gives
\begin{align}
\int\left((-gU_c+aU_c^m)\phi''+bU_c^n\phi''''\right)d\xi
&=\int F''(U)H\phi d\xi
-\left(\phi'''A_1-\phi''A_2+\phi'A_3+\phi A_4\right)\Big|_{\xi=\pm L}.
\end{align}
Hence \(KP(m,n)\) requires exactly the additional trace \(A_4(\pm L)=0\).

For the \(K(m,n)\) exponent criterion,
\begin{align}
A_1&\sim bU_0^n s^{pn},\\
A_2&\sim bpnU_0^n s^{pn-1},\\
A_3&\sim -gU_0s^p+aU_0^m s^{pm}+bpn(pn-1)U_0^n s^{pn-2}.
\end{align}
The first two traces require \(pn>0\) and \(pn>1\). Under these, the only remaining obstruction in \(A_3\) is \(s^{pn-2}\), so all three vanish exactly when \(pn>2\), namely \(p>2/n\).

For \(KP(m,n)\), assume the three \(K\)-traces already vanish, so \(pn>2\). Then \(A_4\to0\) is decided by the three powers in (P6). Either all active leading powers decay separately, or two equal nonpositive leading powers cancel. Separate decay gives the three generic alternatives according to whether \(g=0\), \(g\ne0,m<1\), or \(g\ne0,m>1\). Matching \(p-1=pn-3\) gives the \(g\)-to-dispersion cancellation; matching \(pm-1=pn-3\) gives the nonlinearity-to-dispersion cancellation. Solving the corresponding coefficient equations gives the two displayed amplitudes below. These are exhaustive because, when \(m\ne1\), no other pair of distinct powers can become the unique nondecaying leading order without either separate decay or one of these two equal-power cancellations.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{K(m,n):\quad U_c\text{ is weak}\Longleftrightarrow F'=0\text{ inside and }p>\frac{2}{n}.}
\]
For \(KP(m,n)\), with \(pn>2\), \(A_4(\pm L)=0\) holds exactly in the following six cases:
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
 p>\max\left(\frac1m,\frac3n\right),\quad g=0,\\
 p>\max\left(\frac1m,\frac3n\right),\quad m<1,
 \quad g\ne0,\\
 p>\max\left(1,\frac3n\right),\quad m>1,
 \quad g\ne0,\\
 1\ge p=\frac{2}{n-1},\quad 2m+1>n\ge3,
 \quad g\ne0,
 \quad U_0=\left(\frac{g}{2b}\frac{(n-1)^2}{n(n+1)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{(n-2)(n+1)}},\\
 p=\frac{2}{n-m},\quad n\ge3m,
 \quad g=0,
 \quad U_0=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{\frac{1}{n-m}},\\
 p=\frac{2}{n-m},\quad m+2>n\ge3m,
 \quad g\ne0,
 \quad U_0=\left(-\frac{a}{2b}\frac{(n-m)^2}{n(n+m)}\right)^{\frac{1}{n-m}}.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
The explicit compacton families in the paper can be checked by one catalogue certificate rather than by unrelated substitutions. Let \(T(\xi;\Theta)\) be any one of the goal-listed templates
\[
\begin{gathered}
\alpha(1-\beta\xi^2)^p,
\quad \alpha\cos(\beta\xi)^p,
\quad \alpha\sin(\beta\xi)^p,
\quad \alpha\operatorname{cn}(\beta\xi,k)^p,
\quad \alpha\operatorname{sn}(\beta\xi,k)^p,\\
\alpha\operatorname{cn}(\beta(\xi+L/2),k)^p,
\quad \alpha\operatorname{sn}(\beta(\xi+L),k)^p,
\quad
\alpha\left(\frac{\operatorname{cn}(\beta\xi,k)+\kappa}{\operatorname{cn}(\beta\xi,k)+\gamma}\right)^q.
\end{gathered}
\]
A parameter set \(\Theta\) yields an explicit weak compacton precisely when the interior residual vanishes and the endpoint decision theorem accepts the endpoint exponent. This gives a unified proof strategy for the algebraic, trigonometric, Jacobi-cn, Jacobi-sn, shifted Jacobi, rational Jacobi-cn, antisymmetric, and numerical families required by the goals.

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &R_T(\xi;\Theta):=\left(-gT+aT^m+b(T^n)''\right)'.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &R_T\equiv0\text{ on }(-L,L)
\Longleftrightarrow T\text{ solves the }K(m,n)\text{ traveling-profile ODE.}\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\text{If }T\sim U_0s^p\text{ at }\pm L,
\text{ then }K\text{ weak admissibility is }p>2/n.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{If }T\sim U_0s^p\text{ at }\pm L,
\text{ then }KP\text{ weak admissibility is }p>2/n\text{ plus the }A_4\text{ decision rule.}\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{Strong compactons require the stricter endpoint thresholds }p>3\text{ for }K,
\quad p>4\text{ for }KP.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{For antisymmetric sine or Jacobi profiles, the odd integer or odd rational power condition preserves a real signed profile across zeros.}
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
First, fix a template \(T(\xi;\Theta)\). Substitution into the interior equation produces \(R_T\). Expanding \(R_T\) in a basis of linearly independent \(\xi\)-dependent expressions gives
\[
R_T(\xi;\Theta)=\sum_{j=1}^N q_j(\Theta)E_j(\xi),
\qquad E_1,\ldots,E_N\text{ linearly independent.}
\]
Therefore
\[
R_T\equiv0
\Longleftrightarrow
q_1(\Theta)=\cdots=q_N(\Theta)=0.
\]
This is the algebraic feasibility system for every explicit template. It prevents a low-value catalogue entry: a displayed formula is not accepted because it resembles a compacton, but only because all residual coefficients vanish.

Second, let the endpoint order of \(T\) be \(p_T\), so \(T\sim U_0s^{p_T}\). By the endpoint theorem,
\[
q_1=\cdots=q_N=0\quad\text{and}\quad p_T>\frac2n
\]
is necessary and sufficient for a weak \(K(m,n)\) compacton. For \(KP(m,n)\), the same interior profile transfers only after the fourth trace test accepts:
\[
q_1=\cdots=q_N=0,
\qquad p_T>\frac2n,
\qquad A_4(\pm L)=0.
\]
Thus the catalogue has a common three-part certificate: residual annihilation, endpoint exponent admissibility, and, for \(KP\), the additional \(A_4\) trace.

Third, weak-only entries are identified by comparing endpoint thresholds. For \(K(m,n)\), any accepted template with
\[
\frac2n<p_T\le3
\]
is weak but not strong. For \(KP(m,n)\), any accepted template with
\[
p_T\le4
\]
is weak but not strong. Hence the catalogue does more than list solutions: it separates weak compactons from classical compactons by a checkable exponent gap.

Finally, the numerical family uses the same certificate. With \(V=U^n\), a numerical profile solves the transformed oscillator and then defines \(U=V^{1/n}\). If
\[
V(\pm L)=V'(\pm L)=V''(\pm L)=0,
\]
then \(A_1,A_2,A_3\) vanish for the \(K\) weak trace test. If the additional expression \(A_4(\pm L)\) vanishes, the same numerical cutoff profile passes the \(KP\) weak trace test.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
\text{Explicit catalogue entry accepted}
\Longleftrightarrow
R_T\equiv0\text{ and the relevant endpoint trace test accepts},\\
\text{Weak-only entry}
\Longleftrightarrow
\text{the weak endpoint test accepts but }p_T>3\text{ for }K\text{ or }p_T>4\text{ for }KP\text{ fails},\\
\text{Numerical entry accepted}
\Longleftrightarrow
V\text{ solves the transformed oscillator and its induced }U=V^{1/n}\text{ satisfies the same traces.}
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
The profile
\[
U(\xi)=\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2a}}\cos\left(\frac13\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}\xi\right)
\]
on its positive half-period is a concrete high-value witness: for \(m=n=3\), \(a/b>0\), \(g/a>0\), and \(g\ne0\), the cutoff \(U_c=UH(L-|\xi|)\) is weak but not strong for \(K(3,3)\), and it becomes a weak but not strong \(KP(3,3)\) line compacton under \(\nu=g+\sigma\mu^2\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\lambda:=\frac13\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}},
\qquad K_0:=\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2a}},
\qquad L:=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda},
\qquad U:=K_0\cos(\lambda\xi).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &F(U):=-gU+aU^3+b(U^3)''.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\cos(\lambda\xi)\sim \lambda(L-|\xi|)\quad\text{as }\xi\to\pm L,
\text{ so }p=1.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &K(3,3)\text{ weak endpoint threshold is }p>2/3,
\quad K(3,3)\text{ strong threshold is }p>3.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &KP(3,3)\text{ generic }g\ne0,m>1\text{ endpoint threshold is }p>\max(1,3/n)=1,
\text{ unless a cancellation case applies.}
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
Let \(C=\cos(\lambda\xi)\). Since
\[
(C^3)''=6\lambda^2 C-9\lambda^2 C^3,
\]
we have
\begin{align}
F(U)&=-gK_0C+aK_0^3C^3+bK_0^3(6\lambda^2C-9\lambda^2C^3)\\
&=K_0\left(-g+6bK_0^2\lambda^2\right)C
+K_0^3\left(a-9b\lambda^2\right)C^3.
\end{align}
By the definitions of \(K_0\) and \(\lambda\),
\[
\begin{gathered}
6bK_0^2\lambda^2=g,\\
a-9b\lambda^2=0.
\end{gathered}
\]
Therefore \(F(U)=0\), so \(F'(U)=0\) and \(F''(U)=0\) on \((-L,L)\).

At the endpoints, (P3) gives \(p=1\). Since \(1>2/3\), the three \(K\)-traces \(A_1,A_2,A_3\) vanish and \(U_c\) is a weak \(K(3,3)\) compacton. Since \(1\le3\), it is not strong.

For \(KP(3,3)\), the generic decay threshold is not enough because it would require \(p>1\). However the cancellation case
\[
p=\frac{2}{n-1}=1,
\qquad 2m+1=7>3=n,
\qquad n=3
\]
applies. Its amplitude condition is
\[
U_0=\left(\frac{g}{2b}\frac{(n-1)^2}{n(n+1)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{(n-2)(n+1)}}
=\left(\frac{g}{6b}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The endpoint amplitude of \(U\) is
\[
U_0=K_0\lambda
=\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2a}}\frac13\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}
=\sqrt{\frac{g}{6b}},
\]
so \(A_4(\pm L)=0\). Thus the same cutoff profile is weak for \(KP(3,3)\). Since \(p=1\le4\), it is not strong as a \(KP\) compacton.

Finally, for any \(\mu\in\mathbb R\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), set
\[
\nu:=g+\sigma\mu^2.
\]
Then \(\nu-\sigma\mu^2=g\), so the transferred line wave uses the same profile parameter.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
U_c(\xi)=\sqrt{\frac{3g}{2a}}\cos\left(\frac13\sqrt{\frac{a}{b}}\xi\right)H(L-|\xi|)
\text{ is weak-only for }K(3,3),\\
\nu=g+\sigma\mu^2
\Longrightarrow
u(t,x,y)=U_c(x+\mu y-\nu t)
\text{ is weak-only for }KP(3,3).
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_5:
\section*{Claim}
The transfer from one-dimensional compactons to two-dimensional line compactons is an interior embedding, not an automatic weak-boundary theorem. If
\[
F(U):=-gU+aU^m+b(U^n)'',
\qquad F'(U)=0\quad\text{on }(-L,L),
\]
then every \(\mu\in\mathbb R\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) gives a \(KP(m,n)\) interior line profile after choosing
\[
\nu:=g+\sigma\mu^2.
\]
For cutoff profiles, transfer to a weak \(KP(m,n)\) line compacton holds exactly when the three \(K\)-traces and the additional fourth trace \(A_4=F'\) all vanish at \(\pm L\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &F'(U)=0\quad\text{on }(-L,L).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\xi=x+\mu y-\nu t,
\qquad g_{KP}:=\nu-\sigma\mu^2.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\nu:=g+\sigma\mu^2.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{The }KP(m,n)\text{ line-profile equation is }F_{KP}''(U)=0,
\quad F_{KP}(U):=-g_{KP}U+aU^m+b(U^n)''.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &A_1=bU^n,
\quad A_2=b(U^n)',
\quad A_3=F(U),
\quad A_4=F'(U).\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{The }KP\text{ weak cutoff trace test is }A_1=A_2=A_3=A_4=0\text{ at }\pm L.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
From (P2)--(P3),
\begin{align}
g_{KP}&=\nu-\sigma\mu^2\\
&=(g+\sigma\mu^2)-\sigma\mu^2\\
&=g.
\end{align}
Thus \(F_{KP}=F\). Since \(F'=0\) on \((-L,L)\), differentiating once gives
\begin{align}
F''=0\quad\text{on }(-L,L),
\end{align}
which is exactly the interior \(KP(m,n)\) line-profile equation.

This does not by itself prove weak cutoff transfer. The weak \(K(m,n)\) trace test only checks
\[
A_1(\pm L)=A_2(\pm L)=A_3(\pm L)=0.
\]
The weak \(KP(m,n)\) trace test checks one additional endpoint coefficient multiplying the independent value \(\phi(\pm L)\) after four integrations by parts:
\[
A_4(\pm L)=F'(\pm L)=0.
\]
Therefore the interior implication \(F'=0\Rightarrow F''=0\) must be coupled with the extra endpoint trace to yield a true weak line compacton.

In speed-angle variables, if
\[
c=\frac{\nu}{\sqrt{1+\mu^2}},
\qquad \theta=\arctan(\mu),
\]
then
\begin{align}
g&=\nu-\sigma\mu^2\\
&=c\sqrt{1+\mu^2}-\sigma\mu^2\\
&=c|\sec\theta|-\sigma\tan^2\theta.
\end{align}
This is the same parameter match written in the geometric variables of the line wave.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
F'=0\Longrightarrow F''=0\quad\text{after}\quad \nu=g+\sigma\mu^2,\\
U_c\text{ transfers from weak }K\text{ to weak }KP
\Longleftrightarrow
A_1=A_2=A_3=A_4=0\text{ at }\pm L,\\
g=\nu-\sigma\mu^2=c|\sec\theta|-\sigma\tan^2\theta.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_6:
\section*{Claim}
The transformed variable \(V=U^n\) gives the hidden profile variational principle and the numerical compacton first integral in the same calculation. With
\[
A:=\frac{2na}{(m+n)b},
\qquad
B:=\frac{2ng}{(n+1)b},
\]
the goal-named action
\[
S[V]:=\int_{\mathbb R}\left(-V'^2-A V^{1+m/n}+B V^{1+1/n}+CV\right)d\xi
\]
is the sign-normalised representative of the same stationary principle as
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\left(V'^2+A V^{1+m/n}-B V^{1+1/n}\right)d\xi-C\int_{\mathbb R}Vd\xi,
\]
because multiplication of the Euler equation by a nonzero constant and renaming the arbitrary multiplier \(C\) leaves the stationary profiles unchanged. Its Euler equation is
\[
V''+\frac{a}{b}V^{m/n}-\frac{g}{b}V^{1/n}=\frac{C}{2},
\]
and its first integral is
\[
V'^2=E+CV+B V^{1+1/n}-A V^{1+m/n}.
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align}
\text{(P1)}\quad &U=V^{1/n},
\qquad m,n>0,
\qquad b\ne0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &A=\frac{2na}{(m+n)b},
\qquad B=\frac{2ng}{(n+1)b}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &S[V]=\int \left(-V'^2-A V^{1+m/n}+B V^{1+1/n}+CV\right)d\xi.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{Variations are smooth and compactly supported.}\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{For a numerical weak }K\text{ compacton, }V(\pm L)=V'(\pm L)=V''(\pm L)=0.
\end{align}

\section*{Derivation}
Vary (P3):
\begin{align}
\delta S
&=\int\left(-2V'\delta V'-A\left(1+\frac{m}{n}\right)V^{m/n}\delta V
+B\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)V^{1/n}\delta V+C\delta V\right)d\xi\\
&=\int\left(2V''-A\left(1+\frac{m}{n}\right)V^{m/n}
+B\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)V^{1/n}+C\right)\delta Vd\xi.
\end{align}
Using (P2),
\begin{align}
A\left(1+\frac{m}{n}\right)&=\frac{2a}{b},
&
B\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)&=\frac{2g}{b}.
\end{align}
The Euler equation \(\delta S=0\) is therefore
\begin{align}
2V''-\frac{2a}{b}V^{m/n}+\frac{2g}{b}V^{1/n}+C&=0.
\end{align}
Renaming the arbitrary constant \(C\mapsto -C\) gives
\begin{align}
V''+\frac{a}{b}V^{m/n}-\frac{g}{b}V^{1/n}&=\frac{C}{2}.
\end{align}
Multiply this oscillator equation by \(2V'\):
\begin{align}
2V'V''+\frac{2a}{b}V^{m/n}V'-\frac{2g}{b}V^{1/n}V'&=CV'.
\end{align}
Integrating gives
\begin{align}
V'^2
&=E+CV+\frac{2ng}{(n+1)b}V^{1+1/n}-\frac{2na}{(m+n)b}V^{1+m/n}\\
&=E+CV+B V^{1+1/n}-A V^{1+m/n}.
\end{align}
Conversely, differentiating the first integral recovers the oscillator wherever \(V'\ne0\), and continuity recovers it at turning points when \(V\in C^2\).

Finally, the numerical endpoint condition (P5) is not an arbitrary shooting rule. Since \(U=V^{1/n}\), it enforces the vanishing of the induced weak traces \(A_1,A_2,A_3\) for the \(K(m,n)\) cutoff test; adding \(A_4(\pm L)=0\) upgrades the same numerical profile to the \(KP(m,n)\) weak trace test.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\begin{gathered}
\frac{\delta S}{\delta V}=0
\Longleftrightarrow
V''+\frac{a}{b}V^{m/n}-\frac{g}{b}V^{1/n}=\frac{C}{2},\\
V'^2=E+CV+B V^{1+1/n}-A V^{1+m/n},\\
V\text{ satisfying the oscillator plus endpoint trace conditions gives a numerical weak compacton certificate.}
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
